title: Tail Copter
text: “Father and the others still aren’t back, I say.”
“It’s probably Ren-san taking his sweet time about it.”

Getting dragged around by Hammer Ren—poor thing. But in case something went wrong, I decided to stick my face in the water just to check. I dropped a fire spell in with a splash to see if that hole Father mentioned was really there. Hmm… I could just about make out something that looked like a hole way in the back.
I tried straining my ears to catch the sounds of Father and the others fighting, but underwater, I couldn’t hear much of anything. Eventually, with a splash, Father surfaced with Ren on his back.
“Managed to take it down somehow.”
“…Yeah.”

Once Ren climbed onto the shore, his whole body shook, flinging water everywhere. He was naturally doing that motion Keel does when she gets out of the water. Father called it the “dog drill.” Filolial-sama do it a lot after swimming too.
“Naofumi, you’re awfully skilled at underwater combat.”
“Well, when you spend time with Sadeena-san— you end up going into the sea like it’s a stroll, so you get used to it.”
Big Sister’s Big Sister swims through the sea so effortlessly. Father must be pretty confident in the water too, working well together with Ren in the fight. A bit envious, I say.
“Ren-san. Did you fight well?”
“O-of course I did.”

That was a highly suspicious answer. Father was looking away too, protecting Ren’s pride. Probably couldn’t finish it off with the first strike and had to fire off several skills before finally taking it down. I supposed I should note this as a point of reflection—be careful not to drag Father down, Ren.
“Ren.”
“What?”
“If swimming is so difficult for you, why not spin your tail at high speed and use it as a screw, I say?”
“A tail screw!?”
“Like I could do that!”

I clapped with my ears to demonstrate! Then with a little wiggle, buru-brun! I twisted my ears just slightly and floated up. Just a tiny bit, though. Any more than that and my ears would probably cramp, so I’d need to practice. While fiddling with my ears a bit, I was starting to get the hang of it!
“See, I’m doing it.”
“Motoyasu isn’t human, that’s all! Or are Usaunny monsters or something!”
“Spinning the tail as a screw… using a hero’s enhanced body to forcibly generate thrust—I suppose that’s not entirely implausible?”
“That’s kind of whimsical.”
“Give me a break! Besides, if we’re talking tails, Itsuki’s got the biggest one, so he’d be the better fit! Fly, Itsuki! Naofumi, you go slide across the ground on your belly at high speed!”
“Ah, you’ve dug your own grave here. Might be best not to bring this topic up.”

“High-speed belly sliding, huh… I mean, sure, if I strapped my shield to my stomach and slid across the ground, that’d probably be fast… by the way, apparently squirrel tails can come off if you’re too rough with them, so you shouldn’t treat them carelessly. So don’t try out the Itsuki Tail Copter, okay?”
At Father’s words, all our gazes shifted toward Itsuki’s tail.
“…Naofumi-san. The day is coming soon when I grant you the honor of officially possessing a talent for landing verbal blows.”
“I was trying to defend you, and this is the thanks I get.”
“Motoyasu’s the one who brought it up in the first place! It’s Motoyasu’s fault for floating a little! Stop clapping with your ears!”
Right about then, light shot out from each of our weapons—seemed like they’d been unlocked. Unfortunately, most of what appeared were weapons I already had.
“Enough joking around—there are quite a lot of underwater combat skills and techniques here. Unfortunately, I can’t use any of them right now.”
“I mean… honestly, there are just some deep-sea monsters stronger than Lord of the Sea…”

There was that one time Father and the others went out on a whim with Big Sister’s Big Sister and came back towing a giant deep-sea monster as a souvenir. I remembered it well—people even came from the neighboring town, still under reconstruction, hoping for some of the food.
“…It’s not like I hate looking at the ocean or anything.”
“I know. Once you’re back in your original form, why don’t we go into the sea together with Sadeena-san sometime, Ren?”
“Come to think of it, does Naofumi-san actually go down to the deep sea with Sadeena-san? What about the water pressure and all that?”

Apparently in every world, Father ends up going along with Big Sister’s Big Sister to the deep sea out of sheer social obligation once they get acquainted. Filolial-sama sometimes get taken along too. I recalled going myself, actually.

“Well… without a submarine or anything, there are places you’d think you couldn’t dive into, but it’s not really a problem. There are skills you can unlock on the shield from monsters around there that extend your underwater activity time.”
Now that I think about it, this really is another world, huh, Father said cheerfully.
“Salvaging is pretty interesting too. I mean, tackling dungeons has its own romance to it, but finding a sunken ship and exploring the inside is its own thing.”
“Thanks to the weapons and magic, sure, but still, that’s impressive.”

“True enough. It’s precisely because this is another world. Also, deep-sea fish sometimes have eerie monsters mixed in among them, so it can be scary. Which is also part of what makes it so fantastical.”
“I wonder if there are underwater civilizations somewhere?”
“I feel like I heard something about that around Siltvelt or somewhere… how did that go again?”
“Well, probably falls under the demi-human, beastman category.”
Merfolk and the like, I supposed. Though, they sometimes appear as monsters during wave battles, so it’s hard to tell which is which.
“Underwater cities have a certain romance to them. Kind of want to go see one sometime.”
“Unfortunately, there aren’t any underwater cities in my world either. Same for you, Ren-san, right?”
“Right. Never heard of anything like that, at least.”
“I… feel like I might have heard of one… or maybe not? I say.”
I tried to recall things from back in Japan. Was that from an aquarium? Or something else?
“Honestly, Motoyasu-san’s world sounds more fantastical than some poorly-written isekai.”
“It was just too long ago, so I’ve forgotten, I say.”
“Motoyasu-kun’s looped so many times that things have gotten pretty muddled for him. It’s not strange if his memories get all mixed together.”
“Either way, I get what you’re saying—the sea is full of the unknown.”
“There are aquatic demi-humans and beastmen too, like Sadeena.”

“I heard there are Orca-species and others too. Sadeena-san seems Orca-species-like, but apparently she’s a different species. I think it’s like how ‘orca’ as a single word actually covers several different types.”
That reminded me—Father, back in the very first world, used to talk about orcas from Japan while looking at Big Sister’s Big Sister.
“Talking about the original world, another Father from a different loop mentioned that orcas are apparently divided into four types.”
“Ah, so that topic’s already come up. Their habitats differ, their diets differ. Even the markings differ if you look closely.”
“Naofumi-san, I bet back in your original Japan, you went to aquariums and zoos and bought panda and orca plushies to decorate your room with, didn’t you?”
“No, I’m not that childish, come on. Though I did like animals as much as any normal kid growing up.”

Father’s room topic. The forbidden territory that Big Sister once stumbled into. Once Father realizes this fact, he tends to whip around at incredible speed, so it might be good to hear what kind of reaction gentle Father would have.
“Come to think of it, apparently Big Sister once saw something on Father’s computer in his room, and afterward Father was completely mortified.”
“Eh? Raphtalia-chan saw the contents of my room’s computer?”
At that, Ren and Itsuki both turned to look at him with deeply sympathetic eyes.
“I understand, Naofumi-san. For that kind of material, you really do want a program that self-destructs the computer in case you die, so no one ever sees it.”
“Right. There are absolutely things in one’s personal database that you never want anyone to see.”
“The kind of otaku stuff that’ll kill you if it’s seen. Ren-san, is it your chuunibyou setting documents?”

“No such thing exists. If anything, it’s Itsuki’s chuunibyou materials. I’m sure it’s written somewhere—some delusional novel with a setting about a genius sniper who takes down terrorists from long range after they storm a school.”
Ren and Itsuki fell into a moment of silence—which quickly erupted into a fierce glaring match.
